title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool + parallel calls, result injection, and retries
author: Evan Park
description:
Motivation: callers are increasingly composing multiple tools per request and using parallel tool invocations. We saw two production pain points: (1) inconsistent injection of tool results into follow-up prompts when parallel calls finished out-of-order, and (2) lack of a per-tool retry/backoff policy (causes long-tail failures to surface to users instead of graceful retries). This PR introduces ergonomic improvements to the tool-calling runtime and the OpenAI-compat layer. Summary of changes: - Add deterministic result injection semantics for multi-tool calls: the runtime now supports both ordered and unordered injection modes. By default we preserve the user-declared tool order for injection, but we also provide an opt-in unordered mode for low-latency parallel usage. - Implement per-tool retry policy and light exponential backoff configurable via the tool manifest (retries, initial_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms). Retries are isolated per-tool so a slow/failed tool doesn't block unrelated tool responses. - Add a "result-metadata" envelope for each tool result that includes timing, attempt count, and error-class (transient|permanent). This is surfaced to the OpenAI-compat responses in a non-breaking way. - Streaming stability: when streaming multi-tool responses we now interleave tool-stream frames with stable framing so downstream clients can parse partial results safely. - SDK/compat changes: OpenAI-compat now exposes a tools[] array in the chat completion response when tool results were injected, and includes an optional tool_attempts header. - Tests: unit + integration harness covering ordered/unordered injection, parallel scheduling, and retry semantics. - Docs: API docs updated with examples and migration guidance. Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-6782)
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests added to perf-canary harness
- [x] SDK samples updated (python + ts)
- [x] Backwards-compatible by default (ordered injection preserves existing semantics)
Rollout plan: feature flag gate in runtime (tool_execution_v2). Default enabled for internal QA then staged to 10% of traffic for one week with metrics: tool_success_rate, tool_mean_latency, tool_retry_rate, end_to_end_latency impact. We will monitor for parser compatibility issues in OpenAI-compat clients.

release_notes: Improved tool-calling ergonomics: deterministic result injection modes (ordered by default), per-tool retry/backoff, streaming framing improvements for multi-tool responses, and OpenAI-compat surface for tool attempts and metadata. Backwards-compatible by default. See docs/api/tool-calling.md for migration steps.
